o12.F6a+F6b+F6c+F6d+F6e+F6f.why:
WRONG

The answer key states these are SEM images of single spread cells with cellular processes on pore walls across all six panels, with dense filopodia clearly visible in panel e and the cell in panel a barely distinguishable.

The candidate's per-panel descriptions instead consistently identify the SEM content as fibrous/filamentary structures, fracture or cross-sectional surfaces, coating/substrate interfaces, and membrane/film-like structures — not cells. None of the six panel descriptions mention cells, cell bodies, or filopodia/cellular processes, and the candidate explicitly denies any biological interpretation (e.g., describing ridges, cracks, deposits, striated lamellar bands). This is a direct contradiction of the key's characterization of the imaged subject (cells vs. non-biological fibers/fracture surfaces), not merely a missed detail, so it grades as WRONG rather than PARTIAL.
